headline: Putin-Trump-Xi trilateral summit proposal on Ukraine (APEC Shenzhen, Nov 18-19)
dek: Putin proposed a trilateral Putin-Trump-Xi meeting on the APEC sidelines (Shenzhen, Nov 18-19) to negotiate an end to the Ukraine war on Moscow-favorable terms. China would not object if Trump agrees.
sources: The Wall Street Journal (report); Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov (Monday confirmation); Secretary of State Marco Rubio (Samarkand, acknowledged talks)
fault_line: Should the world's three biggest powers decide Ukraine's future without Kyiv at the table? Yalta 2.0 — or the only deal that can actually stop the war?

sections.what_happened: Putin proposed a trilateral Putin-Trump-Xi meeting on the APEC sidelines (Shenzhen, Nov 18-19) to negotiate an end to the Ukraine war on Moscow-favorable terms. China would not object if Trump agrees. Senior US official: Trump has NOT agreed but could be receptive.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (2026-10-19), AA, Dawn, Hindustan Times, Korea Times, military.com, Daily Pioneer, FreePressJournal, yoopya. Peskov confirmed 'subject was indeed raised, but no specific proposals or agreements were discussed or put forward by anyone'. Rubio confirmed talks ongoing from Samarkand.
sections.what_disputed: Ukrainian FM Andrii Sybiha: a Russia-China-US trilateral 'would do only the opposite: encourage Putin to continue this war'. Zelensky (Bloomberg): accused Trump of trying to force Ukraine's surrender. Peskov himself: 'a final settlement is impossible without the participation of someone in Kyiv.' No date, agenda or guest list agreed — hype risk if framed as a done deal.
sections.why_matters: Moscow is negotiating the end of the war over Kyiv's head — and Washington is warming to it. The deal on the table is the one the battlefield already wrote. Western capitals call it betrayal; the question the video asks is why the peace no one on the front lines opposes is being blocked in Brussels.
sections.context: Background: Putin-Trump-Xi trilateral summit proposal on Ukraine (APEC Shenzhen, Nov 18-19) — NEW Monday

totw_analysis: Our read: Moscow is negotiating the end of the war over Kyiv's head — and Washington is warming to it. The deal on the table is the one the battlefield already wrote. Western capitals call it betrayal; the question the video asks is why the peace no one on the front lines opposes is being blocked in Brussels. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should the world's three biggest powers decide Ukraine's future without Kyiv at the table? Yalta 2.0 — or the only deal that can actually stop the war?
